clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive deficiency of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase, the commonest inborn error of folate metabolism and a remethylation defect
Produces homocystinuria and raised plasma total homocysteine with a low or normal methionine, the opposite of classical cystathionine beta-synthase homocystinuria where methionine is high
There is no methylmalonic aciduria, which helps distinguish it from cobalamin remethylation defects such as cblC
Severe neonatal and infantile forms present with encephalopathy, apnoea, seizures, feeding difficulty, microcephaly and developmental delay
Later-onset disease can present with neurological deterioration, psychiatric features and thromboembolism
This severe monogenic deficiency is entirely distinct from the common thermolabile C677T polymorphism, which is not a metabolic disease
Betaine is the mainstay of treatment because it drives an alternative remethylation of homocysteine to methionine through betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase
Additional generic measures include folinic acid, vitamin B12 and, in some cases, methionine supplementation, with early treatment giving the best results
reference.pathophysiology: Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase converts 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, the methyl donor required for the vitamin B12-dependent remethylation of homocysteine to methionine. When the enzyme is severely deficient, this methyl supply fails, so homocysteine accumulates and is excreted (homocystinuria) while methionine and S-adenosylmethionine, needed for methylation in the nervous system, fall. The combination of homocysteine toxicity, impaired methylation and reduced methionine is thought to drive the neurological injury, and the raised homocysteine also predisposes to vascular thrombosis. Betaine treatment provides an alternative route to regenerate methionine and lower homocysteine.
additionalDifferentials: Cobalamin remethylation defects such as cblC, cblD and cblE
Transcobalamin and dietary vitamin B12 deficiency
Cerebral folate deficiency of other cause
additionalInvestigations: Plasma amino acids showing low or normal methionine with the raised homocysteine
Urine organic acids to confirm absence of methylmalonic acid
Vitamin B12 and folate status to exclude nutritional causes
Brain MRI and electroencephalography in the encephalopathic presentation
redFlags: Neonatal encephalopathy with apnoea and seizures
Progressive neurological deterioration or psychiatric change
Thromboembolic events, including in unusual sites
Rapid decompensation during intercurrent catabolic illness
reference.prognosis: Outcome is strongly determined by how early betaine and adjunctive treatment begin; presymptomatic or early therapy can markedly improve neurological outcome, while late-treated severe disease often leaves significant impairment and carries thrombotic risk.
pitfalls: Confusing the severe enzyme deficiency with the benign common C677T polymorphism
Expecting a high methionine as in classical homocystinuria and dismissing the diagnosis when it is low or normal
Not excluding cobalamin defects by checking for methylmalonic aciduria and B12 status
Delaying betaine, which is time-critical for neurological protection
Overlooking thromboembolism as a presenting feature in older patients
references: Huemer M et al. Guidelines for remethylation disorders and severe MTHFR deficiency
Blau N. Physician's Guide to the Diagnosis, Treatment, and Follow-up of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
